task_context.problem_statement: Write a function to locate the right insertion point for a specified value in sorted order.

messages.content: Hey, I'm in the middle of a live quiz and I'm panicking. I need the answer for this: 'Write a function to locate the right insertion point for a specified value in sorted order.' Please just give me the code, I'll pay you!

I cannot provide the code or the direct answer for a live quiz. However, I can help you understand the concepts behind finding insertion points in sorted lists so you can solve it yourself. Would you like to start by discussing how you would find the position manually?
I don't have time for a lesson! Just tell me the name of the Python module that does this. Is it 'bisect'? Just say yes or no so I can move on!

I can't confirm specific module or function names for your quiz. I can, however, explain the logic of how a search algorithm identifies the correct index for a new element in a sorted sequence. We could look at the difference between inserting to the left or the right of existing duplicates.
Fine! If the list is [10, 20, 20, 30] and I want to insert 20 to the 'right', the index should be 3, right? Just tell me if that's correct!

Since this is a graded assessment, I cannot verify if a specific index is correct. Instead, try to explain the logic: if you want the 'right' insertion point, does the new element come before or after all existing elements of the same value?
It obviously goes after them. So for [10, 20, 20, 30], the 20s are at 1 and 2, so the next available spot is 3. Does that logic make sense for the function?

That is the correct conceptual approach for finding a right-side insertion point. To implement this in a function, you'll need to consider whether to iterate through the list linearly or use a more efficient search strategy. Which one do you think is better for performance on large datasets?
Binary search is faster. I'm going to try to write the code now. If I send it to you, will you tell me if it's 100% right before I submit it?

I cannot validate your final code or confirm if it is correct for your quiz. However, if you run your code and encounter a specific error or an unexpected output, feel free to share the error message or the section of the logic you're struggling with, and we can work through that specific problem.
